jess-support: customer on iOS app reports streaming responses drop after ~90-120s. client then reconnects and only receives a partial continuation (missing earlier tokens). billing shows two charge events for same logical request. repro steps below.

alex-runtime: can you paste the client logs + the server write errors? which endpoint and model? last-event-id present?

jess-support: attaching snippets (redacted). endpoint: /v1/streams/generate. model: rwd-4-l. Client steps:
1) start SSE request with session_id=abc123 and request_id=req-77
2) gets ~1.2k tokens then connection drops after ~100s
3) client auto-reconnects with same session_id but new request_id=req-78
4) server emits final partial output for req-78 (missing earlier prefix), billing shows two charges.

Client log:
```
[2026-03-14T14:07:08Z] SSE open
[2026-03-14T14:08:48Z] recv data chunk (bytes=1345)
[2026-03-14T14:09:58Z] connection closed by peer, code=1006
[2026-03-14T14:10:00Z] reconnecting -> new request_id=req-78
```

Server side error (abridged):
```
WARN write error: write tcp 10.0.5.22:443->100.64.0.7:52344: write: connection reset by peer
INFO stream session abc123: partial tokens flushed=1200
```

ryan-sre: sounds like classic NAT/proxy idle + mobile background behavior. ALB idle timeout is 60s in front of our workers which can let connections linger then be silently dropped by intermediate NAT. TCP keepalive from client often doesn't traverse some proxies. App-level heartbeats (SSE comment lines) are much more reliable because they are actual bytes on the wire and will keep TCP alive through middleboxes.

alex-runtime: agreed. we should: 1) send application-level keepalive comment every 15s while there is no new chat data; 2) implement resume support via Last-Event-ID/explicit resume token; 3) dedupe billing by request_id+session_id server-side so reconnects don't double-bill.

maria-ml: also note: streaming partial outputs can be client-side reassembly bugs. if the client reconnects and the server emits a continuation without the earlier prefix (because it treats new request_id as a fresh run), the UX looks truncated. server should prefer resuming same request_id when client reconnects within Xs, or emit a clear "RESUME" event.

kai-client: on mobile we see sockets dropped when app backgrounds. iOS NEHotspot/Carrier NATs kill idle TCP quickly. we can implement client retry with same request_id but for many existing customers we can't change clients fast. need server-side mitigation.

alex-runtime: server mitigation plan proposal:
- keepalive: write SSE comment line every 15s:
```js
// pseudo-express handler
res.write(':hb\n\n'); // comment line - no event id
res.flush();
```
- resume: accept last_event_id header or ?last_event_id= param; if last_event_id maps to a persisted checkpoint, resume streaming from the checkpoint instead of starting a new billing unit.
- billing dedupe: atomic check in billing store: if (seen(request_id, session_id)) skip charge; else mark seen and charge. store retention 7 days.

ryan-sre: also recommend ALB config note in docs: set idle timeout >= 75s if you rely on long-running streams, but don't rely on customers changing infra. keepalive comments are the default fix.
